definitions.explanation: A story or piece of knowledge that has been passed down orally from generation to generation. Often refers to local legends, folk tales, or traditional beliefs about places, people, or events.

examples.japanese: この{村|むら}には{古|ふる}い{言|い}い{伝|つた}えがある。
examples.english: This village has an old legend.

examples.japanese: {言|い}い{伝|つた}えによると、この{山|やま}には{神|かみ}が{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: According to legend, a god lives in this mountain.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}から{聞|き}いた{言|い}い{伝|つた}えを、{今度|こんど}は{自分|じぶん}の{子供|こども}に{伝|つた}えたい。
examples.english: I want to pass on the stories I heard from my grandmother to my own children.

notes:
USAGE:
{言|い}い{伝|つた}え emphasizes that the story has been passed down orally, distinguishing it from written records. Compare with {伝説|でんせつ} (legend), which is more formal and can refer to famous legends known widely, while {言|い}い{伝|つた}え often refers to local or family oral traditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {言|い}い{伝|つた}えによると: according to legend/tradition
- {古|ふる}い{言|い}い{伝|つた}え: an old legend
- {地元|じもと}の{言|い}い{伝|つた}え: local folklore
- {言|い}い{伝|つた}えが{残|のこ}る: a legend survives/remains
